channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Policy shifts weigh on JPY against US Dollar – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank's Senior Macro Strategist Bas van Geffen discusses renewed Japanese Yen (JPY) weakness following recent joint US-Japan FX intervention that briefly pushed USD/JPY below 156.

item.title: US Dollar: Data-dependent Fed keeps upside in check – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Christopher Wong and Sim Moh Siong note that softer US inflation and debate over the Fed’s reaction function have eroded US Dollar upside momentum, even as the Fed remains data dependent. Upcoming US employment data are seen as critical for policy direction.

item.title: Yen struggles to hold intervention gains and drifts towards 158.00
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) is ticking lower against the US Dollar (USD) on Thursday, trimming gains after an exceptional US-Japan coordinated intervention triggered a 4.5% appreciation late last week.

item.title: Indian Rupee: Policy pause offers limited support – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Charlie Lay reports that the Reserve Bank of India kept the repo rate at 5.25% for a fourth meeting, maintaining a neutral stance. RBI sees recent inflation overshoot as supply-driven and trimmed its FY2026-2027 inflation forecast while lifting growth to 6.7%.

item.title: Czech Koruna: Softer CNB guidance may weigh against euro – ING
item.description: ING strategist Frantisek Taborsky says July Czech inflation at 1.7% year-on-year should have limited impact on the Czech National Bank (CNB) meeting. He expects rates to stay at 3.75%, with guidance leaning more dovish than markets.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver broadly unchanged, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) broadly unchanged on Thursday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $62.01 per troy ounce, broadly unchanged 0.06% from the $62.05 it cost on Wednesday.

item.title: Brazilian Real: Cautious BCB easing offers limited support – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Dev Ashish notes that the central bank of the Brazil, Banco Central do Brasil (BCB) cut the Selic rate by 25bp to 14.0% as expected, extending a 100bp easing cycle since March.

item.title: Swedish Krona: Riksbank set to hold despite core pressure – Nomura
item.description: Nomura strategists highlight that Swedish CPIF ex-energy inflation surprised to the upside in July even as headline CPIF slowed, largely due to government fuel duty cuts and public transport subsidies.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Upside risk while stuck in range against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann highlight USD/JPY traded quietly between 157.27 and 157.87, closing at 157.74, with intraday momentum indicators flat. The pair is expected to stay in a 157.30–158.20 band near term.

item.title: Gold sticks to modest intraday gains, remains below $4,300 amid modest USD strength
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) sticks to modest intraday gains through the first half of the European session, though it remains below the $4,300 mark, or the highest level since June 18, set earlier this Thursday.

item.title: Eurozone Retail Sales declines unexpectedly by 0.3% MoM in June
item.description: Eurozone Retail Sales contracted at a 0.3% pace Month-on-Month (MoM) in June, while they were anticipated to have risen moderately by 0.1%, from 0.4% in May, revised higher from 0.2%.

item.title: United States Dollar Index rebounds following Israeli airstrikes, Jobless Claims eyed
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which measures the value of the US Dollar (USD) against six major currencies, is holding gains after two days of losses and trading around 99.80 during the European session on Thursday.

item.title: Indian Rupee edges lower as oil prices gain ground
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) trades lower against the US Dollar (USD) on Thursday. The USD/INR pair rises to near 95.22 after rebounding from the fresh monthly low of 94.83 posted the previous day.

item.title: Australian Dollar remains depressed; downside seems limited as fiscal concerns weigh on Yen
item.description: The AUD/JPY cross attracts some sellers on Thursday, snapping a two-day winning streak and stalling this week's solid bounce move from its lowest level since late March.

item.title: Equities: Nvidia stands out as broader tech mood cools – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank strategists say the global equity rally lost momentum near record highs as technology shares weakened. The S&P 500 edged lower and the Nasdaq underperformed, with AMD and semiconductor stocks retreating after recent gains.

item.title: Euro holds two-day gains against Yen, investors seek clarity on US-Japan future intervention plans
item.description: The Euro (EUR) clings to two-day gains against the Japanese Yen (JPY) at around 182.25 during the European trading session on Thursday.

item.title: Australian Dollar: RBA uneasy pause – Standard Chartered
item.description: Standard Chartered’s Nicholas Chia expects the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) to keep the cash rate at 4.35% at its 11 August meeting, with no further hikes this year. Q2 core inflation and short-term expectations have eased, while the labour market has softened.

item.title: Canadian Dollar receives support from higher oil prices
item.description: USD/CAD loses ground for the second successive day, trading around 1.4010 during the European hours on Thursday.

item.title: EUR/GBP Price Forecast: Holding below 0.8580 with dips limited so far
item.description: The Euro (EUR) nudges lower against the British Pound (GBP) on Thursday, following a three-day rally. The EUR/GBP remains capped below the late-July top of 0.8586, trading at 0.8575 at the time of writing, yet with downside attempts subdued so far.

item.title: Dow Jones futures gain on tech-driven rally
item.description: Dow Jones futures rise 0.19% to trade around 54,600 during European hours on Thursday. Meanwhile, S&P 500 futures gain 0.09% to trade near 7,760, while Nasdaq 100 futures decline 0.35%, trading near 29,510.

item.title: US Dollar: Wait-and-see mood before payrolls – ING
item.description: ING’s FX Strategist Francesco Pesole notes improved Gulf-related risk sentiment has weighed slightly on the Dollar, but stable Federal Reserve rate expectations remain supportive.

item.title: Gold: Breakout extends as yields ease – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Christopher Wong and Sim Moh Siong highlight a sharp rebound in Gold as easing Middle East tensions weighed on Oil and US Treasury yields, softening the US Dollar.

item.title: British Pound: Gains capped below 1.3555 against US Dollar - UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann report GBP/USD edged higher to 1.3469 after briefly touching 1.3486, with short-term momentum only slightly firmer. The pair is expected to trade in a higher 1.3445–1.3495 range rather than embark on a strong rally.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar stabilizes as markets turn cautious on Mideast uncertainty
item.description: Here is what you need to know on Thursday, August 6:

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: Poised to extend gains beyond 0.8100 amid bullish setup
item.description: The USD/CHF pair attracts some buyers near the 0.8060 region on Thursday amid a modest US Dollar (USD) uptick. Spot prices, for now, seem to have snapped a two-day losing streak and trade around the 0.8080-0.8085 region during the first half of the European session, up nearly 0.15% for the day.

item.title: Australian Dollar eases from highs as the impact from Trade Balance figures fade
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD) posts moderate losses against the US Dollar (USD) on Thursday, retreating to the 0.7040 area from three-week highs at 0.7064 on Wednesday.

item.title: Euro: Oil-price sensitivity and war-end effects – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Michael Pfister argues that lower Oil prices can initially restrain the Euro (EUR) by reducing European Central Bank (ECB) rate expectations.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar slips under safe-haven US Dollar surge
item.description: NZD/USD extends its losses for the second successive day, trading around 0.5870 during the European hours on Thursday. The pair depreciates as the US Dollar (USD) gains support from renewed safe-haven demand following an Israeli airstrike in southern Lebanon.

item.title: GBP/USD Price Forecast: Gathers strength for VCP breakout
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) trades marginally lower at around 1.3460 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Thursday.

item.title: Indian Rupee: Gradual strengthening path outlined – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Michael Wan expects USD/INR to grind lower over the next 3–6 months towards 94.00, before rebounding to 96.00 in the next calendar year.
